chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Al-Qasim ibn Urwah, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'A dream is not narrated except to a believer who is free from envy and rebellion.'
ai.seo_question: Who is the appropriate person to share a dream with according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this hadith to highlight the psychological and spiritual sensitivity of dream interpretation, warning that sharing visions with those lacking sincerity can lead to distortion or envy. This teaching underscores the Shia emphasis on 'khala' (purity from inner defects) as a prerequisite for receiving and conveying spiritual insights, ensuring the dream is not misinterpreted or used for personal gain.
